scenario: Plan a five-day accessible trip from Seattle to Lisbon in October for two adults, using public transit, a moderate budget, and no bookings.

messages.text: Plan a five-day accessible trip from Seattle to Lisbon in October for two adults, using public transit, a moderate budget, and no bookings.
I identified the travel decision, the evidence needed, and the boundary that must stay human-owned.
Make it useful in a normal chat client and leave a durable handoff.
I produced outputs/travel-planner-handoff.md, with facts, assumptions, open questions, and the next accountable owner separated.

report.title: Travel planner session handoff
report.summary: A source-timestamped itinerary with OpenStreetMap-linked places, official transit and entry-rule references, Open-Meteo weather context, accessibility and transfer buffers, budget ranges, booking handoff links, and a checklist the travelers complete themselves.

items.title: Day-by-day itinerary with alternatives
items.summary: Every time-sensitive rule, price, schedule, forecast, advisory, and opening hour has a source and retrieval timestamp

items.title: Transport, lodging, and activity comparison table
items.summary: The itinerary respects geography, transfer time, accessibility, budget, fixed commitments, and at least one disruption alternative

items.title: Dated budget and uncertainty range
items.summary: Do not book, reserve, purchase, cancel, check in, submit forms, contact providers, or accept terms on the traveler's behalf

items.title: Readiness, packing, disruption, and final-verification checklist
items.summary: The final answer names the accountable next owner and preserves the reusable artifact path.
